kpis.sub: MP FALLS TOWARD ITS 52-WEEK LOW AS THE RARE-EARTH SELLOFF EXTENDS (OCT 15 CLOSE)
kpis.label: MP Materials traded ~$40.17 on Oct 15 (-3.5% on the day), down from $46.15 on Oct 9 and only ~6% above its $37.81 52-week low (high $100.25). USAR is down ~31% over the past month to ~$10.54, and REMX closed Oct 16 at $54.23, below the prior-week one-year low and near the bottom of a $53.75–$111.55 range (-29% over 12 months). MP and USAR each fell ~6% on Oct 12. The Nov 5 Q3 report (after the close) is confirmed. MP also sits in the Robotics sleeve — don't double-count

kpis.sub: CHINA'S EXPORT-CONTROL SUSPENSION STILL RUNS TO JAN 10 — NO NEW TERMS SINCE
kpis.label: The US-China truce, including suspension of Beijing's Oct 2025 rare-earth controls, runs to Jan 10, 2027 after the Sep 23 two-month extension. China's April 2025 licensing regime was never lifted, and Benchmark notes the official US summary of the May Trump–Xi meeting dropped earlier language about China 'effectively eliminating' controls, read as acceptance that licensing stays. Rare-earth equities have kept falling regardless, so the market is pricing a thaw, not a structural fix

kpis.sub: LITHIUM CARBONATE DOWN ~23% IN A MONTH TO A ~TEN-MONTH LOW (OCT 16)
kpis.label: China lithium carbonate fell 2.2% on Oct 16 to CNY 102,150/t, down ~23% over a month and roughly at the CNY 100,000 level Trading Economics calls the lowest in nearly ten months. SMM's revised inventory method added ~175,000t to estimated Chinese stockpiles, and Mineral Resources restarted Bald Hill while Core Lithium restarted Finniss, feeding 2027 glut fears. Albemarle closed $95.48 on Oct 16 (-2.75%) and LIT $64.05; Lithium Americas $2.18, below its prior 52-week low

kpis.sub: COMEX COPPER ~5% BELOW THE SEPTEMBER RECORD AS CHILEAN STRIKES PERSIST (OCT 18)
kpis.label: Copper was $6.53/lb on Oct 18, down 2.4% over a month but up ~30% year over year, against a $6.85 record set in September. Strikes at Antofagasta's Centinela and BHP's Escondida plus weather at Codelco's El Teniente tighten supply, while a stronger-than-expected US inflation print raised rate-hike fears. Freeport closed $69.54 on Oct 16 (-0.7%), down from $73.68 a week earlier, as miners sold off with the Nasdaq (-2.1%)

themes.title: The Jan 10, 2027 cliff is unchanged — and the scarcity premium keeps deflating
themes.description: Nothing new on the China front this week: the suspension of Beijing's Oct 2025 controls lapses Jan 10, 2027, the April 2025 seven-element licensing remains, and Benchmark reads the May summit summary as accepting that licensing stays. Rare-earth equities nonetheless extended their month-long slide (USAR -31% in a month, REMX at a one-year low), so the market is pricing a thaw rather than any structural change in Western separation and magnet capacity.

themes.title: A presidential post on Greenland exploration lifts CRML — but names no project
themes.description: On Oct 14 Trump posted that large oil, gas and mineral exploration was preparing to begin in Greenland, lifting Critical Metals ~4–5%. No project, operator, permit or timetable was named, and Tanbreez was not mentioned. It follows the Sep 22 US–Denmark–Greenland security agreement and is a sentiment tailwind, not an award.

themes.title: USAR's government funding is milestone-based — and juniors are tapping equity markets
themes.description: USA Rare Earth's federal support arrives in stages as construction and production targets are met, so the next test is hitting upcoming construction milestones. Energy Fuels announced a $500M at-the-market equity programme (shares fell nearly 10%) and drew law-firm investor probes, a reminder that Vault, EXIM and DoD backstops favour projects with product, while juniors fund themselves by dilution.

themes.title: Lynas buys Meteoric Resources to add Brazil's Caldeira ionic-clay project
themes.description: Lynas agreed an all-scrip deal for Meteoric Resources (reported at roughly A$968M by one source), adding the Caldeira project in Brazil. Lynas posted FY26 revenue of A$978M (+76%) and net income of A$222M, yet the shares (A$12.40 on Oct 8) sit near their A$12.15 52-week low, showing the market is not paying for growth while NdPr prices stay depressed.

bear_case.title: The premium keeps deflating faster than the supply chain is built
bear_case.description: Even with the truce extended to Jan 10, REMX closed at $54.23 on Oct 16 (-29% over a year), MP is ~60% below its $100.25 high near ~$40, and USAR fell ~31% in a month. MP remains loss-making at the EPS line on a high price-to-sales multiple, and Western separation, metallization and magnet capacity is thin. Selling pressure has persisted with no company-specific news (Oct 7, Oct 12).

bear_case.title: Commodity cycles cut both ways
bear_case.description: Lithium carbonate has fallen ~23% in a month to ~CNY 102k/t with Bald Hill and Finniss restarts and a larger estimate of Chinese stockpiles; Albemarle ($95.48) and Lithium Americas ($2.18) reflect it. Copper sits near records, so Freeport's earnings are cycle-high even as the shares fell to $69.54. A producer can be an excellent business at the wrong point in its price cycle.

bear_case.title: China can flood, freeze or consolidate
bear_case.description: Beijing's controls are suspended, not repealed: they can return Jan 10, 2027 and April 2025 licensing remains in force. A flood of cheap Chinese NdPr would undercut non-Chinese producers even with Pentagon price floors, which only protect projects that already have product. Lynas's record output at 70% of NdPr nameplate shows how depressed prices bite.

bear_case.title: Junior dilution, milestone funding and policy dependency
bear_case.description: Energy Fuels' $500M at-the-market programme cut the shares ~10% and attracted investor-rights law-firm probes; USAR's federal money is paid only on milestones; CRML has going-concern doubt and no revenue. Vault, EXIM, DoD floors and the House package are real but discretionary, and H.R. 4090 still has to clear the Senate.

stance.basis: Weights are a share of a hypothetical 100% sleeve for THIS SECTOR only — not a share of your portfolio. Core and Speculative names carry the weight; Watch and Avoid deliberately carry 0% because the point of those groups is that you are not holding them yet.

positions.name: MP Materials
positions.note: Still the only US mine-to-magnet producer with Apple and DoD anchors and Q2 revenue up 89% to $108.5M, but at ~$40 (down from $46 a week ago, ~6% above its $37.81 low) with Q3 due Nov 5 it is held as Core on business quality, not price. Also sits in the Robotics sleeve — don't double-count.

positions.name: USA Rare Earth
positions.note: Blacksburg construction and the Serra Verde deal are real, but at ~$10.54 (-31% in a month, through its prior $11.45 low) with milestone-based federal funding still ahead, this is optionality with a genuine chance of zero.

positions.name: Lithium Americas
positions.note: Thacker Pass is still the largest US lithium build and Canaccord upgraded to Speculative Buy, but at $2.18 (near its $2.04 52-week low) with lithium carbonate down ~23% in a month the size stays the smallest in the sleeve.

positions.name: Freeport-McMoRan
positions.note: Excellent copper business, but copper at $6.53/lb is still ~5% off a September record, Grasberg is still recovering and the shares ($69.54) trade with the Nasdaq tape — a late-cycle price with an unresolved tariff decision, not an entry point.

positions.name: Albemarle
positions.note: Lithium carbonate fell ~23% in a month to ~CNY 102k/t on restarts and a larger Chinese stockpile estimate; with ALB at $95.48 the cycle has not clearly bottomed, and Q3 on Nov 4 plus a CEO arriving Feb 2027 leave too many open questions.

positions.name: Lynas Rare Earths
positions.note: FY26 revenue A$978M (+76%) and a record 13,089t REO, but NdPr ran 7,260t vs 10,500t nameplate in a depressed price market and the Meteoric scrip takeover adds integration risk at A$12.40 near its 52-week low — good business, unresolved question.

positions.name: Energy Fuels
positions.note: A $500M at-the-market programme (shares -~10%) plus law-firm investor probes on Oct 14–15 put dilution and governance questions ahead of a still-unprofitable rare-earth ramp at $8.47, near the $7.81 low.

positions.name: Critical Metals
positions.note: Roughly $2M of exploration revenue, substantial going-concern doubt and no producing asset; the Oct 14 Greenland post lifted the shares ~4–5% without naming Tanbreez, so the research does not support owning it.
